text: A generator produces values one at a time instead of building a whole list up front.
Countdown looks like a normal function, right up until you spot the yield.
While n is greater than zero we yield n — and yield is the key word here.
Yield hands a value back and pauses the function, keeping every local variable alive.
The next time you ask for a value it resumes on the very next line and decrements n.
Once the loop finally ends, we sneak in one last yield, the string liftoff.
A for loop just keeps pulling values until the generator is exhausted.
Three, two, one, liftoff — each one arriving only when it's asked for.
No list is ever built in memory, which is why this scales to millions of items.
